chapter.v:
A kind
reply wards off anger, but hurtful words make people mad.

What wise
people say makes knowledge attractive, but stupid people talk a lot of nonsense.

The Lord
sees everywhere, watching the evil and the good.

Gentle words
are a source of life, but telling lies does a lot of damage.

Only a
foolish son despises his father's instruction, but one who accepts correction is sensible.

There's plenty
of treasure where good people live, but the income of the wicked brings them trouble.

Wise people
share their knowledge, but stupid people don't think like that.

The Lord
hates the sacrifices of the wicked, but he loves the prayers of the good.

The Lord
hates the ways of the wicked, but he loves those who do what is right.

If you
leave the right path you will be severely disciplined; anyone who hates correction will die.

Those already
dead have no secrets from the Lord—how much more does he know our thoughts!

Scoffers don't
like to be corrected, so they don't go to the wise for advice.

If you're
happy inside, you'll have a cheerful face, but if you're sad, you look crushed.

An insightful
mind looks for knowledge, but stupid people feed on foolishness.

The life
of poor people is hard, but if you stay cheerful, it's a continual feast.

It's better
to respect the Lord and only have a little than to have plenty of money and the trouble that comes with it.

Better a
dinner of vegetables where there's love than eating meat with hatred.

Short-tempered people
stir up trouble, but those slow to anger calm things down.

The way
of lazy people is overgrown with thorns, but the path of the good is an open highway.

A wise
son makes his father happy, but a stupid man despises his mother.

Stupidity makes
people with no sense happy, but sensible people do what is right.

Plans fall
apart without good advice, but with plenty of advisors they're successful.

A good
answer makes people happy—it's great to say the right thing at the right moment!

Life's path
for the wise leads upwards, so that they can avoid the grave below.

The Lord
pulls down the house of the proud, but he protects the boundaries of the widow's property.

The Lord
hates the thoughts of the wicked, but he honors the words of the pure.

People greedy
for ill-gotten gains make trouble for their families, but those who hate bribes will live.

Good people
think how best to answer questions, but stupid people say all kinds of evil things.

The Lord
keeps his distance from the wicked, but he hears the prayers of the good.

Bright eyes
make you happy, and good news makes you feel good.

If you
pay attention to positive advice you'll be one of the wise.

If you
ignore instruction you have no self-esteem, but if you listen to correction you gain understanding.

Respect for
the Lord teaches wisdom; humility goes before honor.
